title: Coroots separate vectors in the integral root span
statement: Let $M,N$ be free $\mathbf Z$-modules with finite bases [def-weil-pbc-free-module], in a perfect bilinear pairing $\langle-,-\rangle:M\times N\to\mathbf Z$, meaning that the induced maps $M\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(N,\mathbf Z)$ and $N\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(M,\mathbf Z)$ are isomorphisms. Let $I$ be finite and let $a:I\hookrightarrow M$ and $c:I\hookrightarrow N$ be injective maps. Suppose $\langle a_i,c_i\rangle=2$ and, for every $i\in I$, there is a permutation $\sigma_i:I\simeq I$ such that, for all $j\in I$, $$a_{\sigma_i(j)}=a_j-\langle a_j,c_i\rangle a_i,\qquad c_{\sigma_i(j)}=c_j-\langle a_i,c_j\rangle c_i.$$ Put $Q=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Z}\{a_i:i\in I\}\subseteq M$ [def-weil-submodule-span]. For every $x\in Q$ with $x\ne0$, there exists $i\in I$ such that $\langle x,c_i\rangle\ne0$. No spanning or reducedness assumption on the two families is imposed; $I=\varnothing$ is allowed.

source.place: Appendix C.44, printed p.618: nondegeneracy of the root/coroot rational-span pairing, restricted to the root lattice; C.37--C.43 give the self-dual axioms and proof. Integer-root-pairing formulation: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Finite/Nondegenerate.lean, RootPairing.exists_coroot_ne, lines 181--188.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: take R = S = integers, I the given finite index type, P.root = a, P.coroot = c and P.reflectionPerm = sigma (RootPairing fields, Defs.lean:82--98); apply P.exists_coroot_ne integers to x in P.rootSpan integers. The automatic IsValuedIn-self instance is IsValuedIn.lean:62, hence P.IsCrystallographic; instIsAnisotropicOfIsCrystallographic at Nondegenerate.lean:87 supplies IsAnisotropic. rootSpan is the integer span by IsValuedIn.lean:166, and algebraMap_coroot'In_apply at IsValuedIn.lean:224 identifies its conclusion with the displayed evaluation since the integer algebra map is the identity. Read Nondegenerate.lean:147--188, including the full hypotheses. No IsRootSystem, IsReduced, Nonempty I or finiteness of the Weyl group is assumed.
